title: Pass 3 reference table: 3D cylindrical fat-pad / spherical mesenchymal BARW with anisotropic ECM fiber alignment and inflationary domain growth (Bordeu et al. 2023), plus clonal neutral-drift dynamics inside terminal end buds (Scheele et al. 2017) coupled to the BARW tree

sources.citation: Hannezo E, Scheele CLGJ, Moad M, Drogo N, Heer R, Sampogna RV, van Rheenen J, Simons BD (2017). A Unifying Theory of Branching Morphogenesis. Cell 171(1):242-255.e27.
sources.used_for: BARW rules (A -> 2A, A -> A + I, A + I -> I); quasi-2D mammary fat pad vs 3D kidney/pancreas mesenchyme; critical Galton-Watson subtree statistics P(S) ~ S^(-3/2); q_branch -> 1/2.

sources.citation: Scheele CLGJ, Hannezo E, Muraro MJ, Zomer A, Langedijk NSM, van Oudenaarden A, Simons BD, van Rheenen J (2017). Identity and dynamics of mammary stem cells during branching morphogenesis. Nature 542(7641):313-317.
sources.used_for: Equipotent mammary stem cells in terminal end buds (TEBs) undergo neutral drift; clone fate (loss vs expansion) is dictated by TEB bifurcation / termination; labelled clones become confined to subtrees of the ductal network.

sources.citation: Bordeu I, Chatzeli L, Simons BD (2023). Inflationary theory of branching morphogenesis in the mouse salivary gland. Nature Communications 14:3422.
sources.used_for: 3D BARW in a growing (inflating) mesenchymal domain; tips and ducts embedded in an anisotropic ECM / mesenchyme; motivation for the inflation_rate parameter and the ECM fiber-alignment torque.

sources.citation: Moran PAP (1958). Random processes in genetics. Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society 54(1):60-71.
sources.used_for: Moran birth-death process used for neutral drift of labelled cells inside a fixed-size TEB stem-cell pool.

sources.citation: Klein AM, Simons BD (2011). Universal patterns of stem cell fate in cycling adult tissues. Development 138(15):3103-3111.
sources.used_for: Neutral-drift clone-size scaling and the martingale (conserved mean labelled fraction) property of neutral competition.

cylinder_fat_pad.description: Reduced model of the pubertal mouse mammary fat pad: a cylinder of radius R_c and length L_c (in units where the tip speed v_0 = 1 and the branch length l_b = v_0/k_b = 8.33); the primary duct enters at one end and grows along +z.
cylinder_fat_pad.note: Hannezo et al. (2017) treat the mammary fat pad as quasi-2D and elongated; the 3D cylinder here is the simplest honest 3D fat-pad reduction. Ducts outside the cylinder annihilate at the capsule.

sphere_mesenchyme.description: Reduced model of embryonic mesenchyme (metanephric kidney / salivary gland): a sphere of radius R_s(t) that may inflate in time, R_s(t) = R_s(0) * (1 + inflation_rate * t) (Bordeu et al. 2023 inflationary BARW).
sphere_mesenchyme.note: Bordeu et al. (2023) also advect already-deposited ducts with the inflating domain; here only the capsule boundary inflates (residual carried to Pass 4).

ecm_anisotropy.description: Nematic ECM fiber-alignment torque on the tip direction u: du = lambda * (f . u) * (f - (f . u) u) dt, which rotates u toward +/- f (the fiber axis). lambda = 0 is isotropic matrix.
ecm_anisotropy.sweep_design: paired: identical PRNG seed for every lambda within a geometry so that the S(lambda) comparison is paired; chi = 0.14 in the cylinder is the same polar distal bias used by the 2D simulator, so the S = 0 isotropic reference applies to the chi = 0, lambda = 0 control
ecm_anisotropy.expected_qualitative_result: S increases monotonically with lambda; at lambda >= 0.4 (alignment time 1/lambda << l_b) sibling tips realign to the fiber axis within R_a of each other and annihilate, collapsing the tree (alignment-induced sibling annihilation)
ecm_anisotropy.nematic_order_parameter: S = < (3 cos^2 theta - 1) / 2 > over ductal segments, theta = angle between segment direction and fiber axis f (length-weighted)

clonal_neutral_drift.description: Each active tip (TEB) carries a pool of N_teb equipotent stem cells of which k are labelled (Scheele et al. 2017). Along a ductal segment the pool undergoes Moran birth-death steps at rate rho per unit duct length: k -> k + 1 or k -> k - 1 each with probability k (N - k) / N^2, otherwise k unchanged. At a bifurcation (A -> 2A) the N cells are split hypergeometrically into two halves of N/2 and each daughter TEB doubles back to N (labelled count 2 k_1 and 2 (k - k_1)). At annihilation (A + I -> I) the pool differentiates into duct; the deposited duct inherits the TEB labelled fraction k/N.

reference_values.martingale_note: E[k_{t+1} | k_t] = k_t for Moran steps and E[2 k_1] = k for the hypergeometric split (Lean Theorems 4-5); therefore the duct-length-weighted labelled fraction of the whole tree is an unbiased estimator of the initial fraction 0.125.
reference_values.single_cell_clone_fixation_probability_t: 1 / N_teb = 0.015625 for a clone that stays in one TEB long enough to fix (Moran); in a finite BARW tree most clones are lost or diluted by splitting before fixation.
reference_values.clone_size_tail_note: Scheele et al. (2017): mammary clone sizes are set by the branching-tree statistics; a labelled lineage that survives spans a critical Galton-Watson subtree, so the number of labelled ductal segments per clone inherits the P(S) ~ S^(-3/2) tail.

unsourced_constants: n_cells_per_teb = 64 is a reduced free parameter (real TEBs contain of order 10^2 cells; no value is taken from a figure/table)
moran_rate_per_unit_length = 1.0 is a free parameter in simulation units
